cases.title: 안경 beginning with the surname 안
cases.why: 안경 ('glasses') starts with the surname 안.

ambiguity.note: An accessory that is taken off.

cases.title: 박물관 beginning with the surname 박
cases.why: 박물관 ('museum') starts with the common surname 박 and is a long word, so a prefix lookup of two or three syllables misfires.

ambiguity.note: A museum is a venue that closes on a given day.

cases.title: 최고 beginning with the surname 최
cases.why: 최고 ('the best') starts with the common surname 최 and ends with a particle-like syllable 의 after it.

ambiguity.note: 'The best in the industry' is a superlative.

cases.title: 최근 beginning with the surname 최
cases.why: 최근 ('recently') starts with the surname 최 and is one of the most frequent adverbs.

ambiguity.note: A time adverb followed by the locative-like particle 에.

cases.title: Name ending in 도 followed by the additive particle 도
cases.why: Names ending in 도 followed by the additive particle 도 produce 도도; only the second is the particle.

cases.title: Name ending in 은 followed by the subject marker 이
cases.why: A name ending in 은 takes the consonant-final subject marker 이; the 은 inside the name stays in the span.

cases.title: Name ending in 은 followed by the topic marker 은
cases.why: The name 최아은 ends in the syllable 은, which is also the topic marker. Dropping a final 은 as a particle removes a real name syllable; the span must be 최아은 and only the second 은 is the particle.

cases.title: Name ending in 가 followed by the subject marker 가
cases.why: A name ending in 가 takes 가 as a subject marker, leaving 가가; only the second 가 is the particle.

cases.title: Name ending in 이 followed by the subject marker 가
cases.why: The name 김하이 ends in 이, which is also a subject marker; the vowel-final name takes 가 and 이 stays in the span.

cases.title: Name ending in 이 followed by the topic marker 는
cases.why: Same trap with a different particle: 이 inside the name, 는 as the particle.

cases.title: 강아지 beginning with the surname 강
cases.why: 강아지 ('puppy') starts with the surname 강.

ambiguity.note: A puppy playing in a yard is an animal.

cases.title: Full name 김치우 whose first two syllables spell 김치
cases.why: 김치우 is a plausible person name (surname 김, given name 치우) but its first two syllables spell the word for kimchi. A word-lookup approach can split it as 김치 + 우 and miss the person.

ambiguity.note: Arriving first is a human action and the string is a plausible full name, though 김치 is also the word for kimchi.

cases.title: 김밥 as lunch
cases.why: Another common food word beginning with the surname 김; a prefix lookup on surnames misfires on it.

ambiguity.note: 김밥 is a food item and the object of 'ate'.

cases.title: 김치찌개 begins with the most common surname 김
cases.why: 김 is the most common Korean surname and begins the word for kimchi. A detector that fires on a surname character followed by anything produces a false positive on the dish name.

ambiguity.note: The compound 김치찌개 names a dish; 김 is only the first syllable of the word 김치 (kimchi).

cases.title: 김장 beginning with the surname 김
cases.why: 김장 ('making kimchi for winter') starts with the most common surname 김.

ambiguity.note: 김장 is a seasonal household activity described with a seasonal predicate.

cases.title: 김 meaning dried seaweed (laver)
cases.why: The same syllable as a food ingredient, with the object marker 을; an adjective 마른 ('dried') modifies it.

ambiguity.note: 'Dried' and 'roasted' show it is the food ingredient laver.

cases.title: 김 meaning steam, followed by the subject marker 이
cases.why: The standalone noun 김 ('steam') followed by 이 looks exactly like a one-syllable name with a particle. This is the hardest false-positive trap for a surname-only reading.

ambiguity.note: 'Steam rising from the soup' is a physical phenomenon; the noun 김 takes the subject particle 이.

cases.title: 권리 beginning with the surname 권
cases.why: 권리 ('right/entitlement') starts with the surname 권.

ambiguity.note: An abstract noun in a legal-style statement.

cases.title: 한번 beginning with the surname 한
cases.why: 한번 ('once, for a time') starts with the surname 한.

ambiguity.note: An adverb attached to an imperative verb.

cases.title: 임금 beginning with the surname 임
cases.why: 임금 means both 'wages' and 'king'; it begins with the surname 임.

ambiguity.note: 'Rose this year' selects the wage meaning.

cases.title: 정부 beginning with the surname 정
cases.why: 정부 ('government') starts with 정 and is an institution word.

ambiguity.note: 정부 is an institution that announces policy.

cases.title: 정말 beginning with the surname 정
cases.why: 정말 ('really') starts with the common surname 정.

ambiguity.note: 정말 is an adverb of degree.

cases.title: 정원 as a garden
cases.why: 정원 means 'garden' (and also 'capacity') and is a given name; a plant description selects the noun.

ambiguity.note: Flowers bloom in a garden.

cases.title: 조금 beginning with the surname 조
cases.why: 조금 ('a little') starts with the surname 조, which is also a counter and a prefix in many words.

ambiguity.note: 조금 is a quantity adverb followed by the restrictive 만.

cases.title: 조용히 beginning with the surname 조
cases.why: 조용히 ('quietly') starts with the surname 조.

ambiguity.note: An adverb of manner describing how the children sat.

cases.title: 문제 beginning with the surname 문
cases.why: 문제 ('problem') starts with the surname 문 and is extremely frequent.

ambiguity.note: A problem that is unresolved, preceded by the demonstrative 이.

cases.title: 남자 beginning with the surname 남
cases.why: 남자 ('man') starts with the surname 남 and is a very frequent generic noun.

ambiguity.note: A generic noun for a man modified by a demonstrative.

cases.title: 배우진 as a person name
cases.why: Partner of word-actor-versus-name-baeu: a person name that begins with 배우.

ambiguity.note: 배우진 alone is the ordinary noun for a cast; the honorific 씨 after it selects a person, and the subject marker 가 follows 씨.

cases.title: 정부영 as a person name
cases.why: Partner of word-government-versus-name-jeongbu: a person whose name starts with the same two syllables; the full three-syllable string is the span.

ambiguity.note: The three-syllable string followed by the subject marker 이 is a person; 정부 alone would take 가.

cases.title: 조사랑 as a person name
cases.why: Partner of word-survey-versus-name-josa: a three-syllable name starting with 조사.

ambiguity.note: The subject marker 이 attaches to the three-syllable name; 조사 as a noun would not take 이 here.

cases.title: 노래 beginning with the surname 노
cases.why: 노래 ('song') starts with the surname 노 and is a very frequent everyday noun.

ambiguity.note: A song is sung; 노래 is the object noun.

cases.title: 오이 as the vegetable 'cucumber'
cases.why: 오이 is a vegetable and equals the surname 오 plus the particle-like syllable 이.

ambiguity.note: Slicing for a salad selects the vegetable.

cases.title: A person receiving applause
cases.why: 박수 is the word for 'applause' and begins with the common surname 박. The sentence holds both the full name 박수진 and the noun 박수.

ambiguity.note: 박수진 is a full name and subject; 박수 is the object noun 'applause'.

cases.title: A person who bought gimbap
cases.why: A sentence that holds a real full name and the food word 김밥, both starting with 김. Exactly one of the two is a person.

ambiguity.note: 김민수 is a three-syllable full name; 김밥 is a food noun that follows it as the object.

cases.title: 신발 beginning with the surname 신
cases.why: 신발 ('shoes') starts with the surname 신 and is a very frequent everyday noun.

ambiguity.note: Shoes are taken off when entering.

cases.title: 송아지 beginning with the surname 송
cases.why: 송아지 ('calf') starts with the surname 송 and is an ordinary animal noun.

ambiguity.note: An animal born on a farm.

cases.title: 배우 as 'actor'
cases.why: 배 is a surname and 배우 is the ordinary word 'actor'.

ambiguity.note: Going on stage is predicated of a performer; 배우 is the occupation noun.

cases.title: 정부 as 'government'
cases.why: 정 is a surname and 정부 is the ordinary word 'government'. A surname-initial heuristic fires here.

ambiguity.note: Announcing a policy is predicated of a state institution.

cases.title: 조사 as 'survey'
cases.why: 조 is a surname and 조사 is the ordinary word 'survey/investigation'.

ambiguity.note: A result of a survey is a nominal compound with 결과.

cases.title: 이 as the demonstrative 'this' before 사람
cases.why: 이 is both a very common surname and the demonstrative 'this'. Followed by 사람 ('person') it is the demonstrative, not a surname.

ambiguity.note: 'This person' is a demonstrative plus noun.

cases.title: 이 as the numeral two
cases.why: The Sino-Korean numeral 이 ('two') is the same syllable as the surname 이.

ambiguity.note: 'Two plus three is five' is arithmetic.

cases.title: 윤리 beginning with the surname 윤
cases.why: 윤리 ('ethics') starts with the surname 윤.

ambiguity.note: 연구 윤리 is a noun phrase; 윤리 is an abstract noun.

cases.title: 윤기: a gloss noun that is also a given name
cases.why: 윤기 ('shine/gloss') is also a given name. In a description of hair it is a noun.

ambiguity.note: A physical property of hair; the noun is the subject of 'flows'.
